clues.title: Highway markers
text: If you see black-and-white highway markers, you're in Argentina.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: License plate
text: Old license plates in Argentina have a black dot in the middle of a white plate, which is easy to spot. New license plates are fully white with a blue line at the top, similar to those in Brazil.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Double concrete pole
text: This double-rounded concrete pole connected by a concrete ring is almost exclusive to Argentina. Similar ones can occasionally be found in Bolivia, but the landscape will be vastly different.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape + black car
text: If you find yourself in a flat, desolate, treeless, sparsely populated area with a visible black back of the Google car, you're likely in Argentina.
(Jordan might resemble this landscape for new players, and it also has a black back on the car, so be aware of that.)
(Only other countries in South America with car like that are: Peru and Uruguay)

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: La Rioja red mountains
text: In La Rioja, just north of Talampaya National Park, there is a part of the RN40 with almost blindingly bright red mountains. Good luck telling it apart from similar roads in Catamarca and Salta! The best method may be the clouds: This road has low clouds toward the South (except when it doesn't), while the one in Catamarca is always cloudless and the one in Salta has higher, better defined clouds. It's tough.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Catamarca red mountains
text: On the 60, east of Fiambalá, bright red mountains line the road, sometimes quite dramatically. A few of the red hills are embedded in between gray hills in a way that almost looks like a badly colored black and white photograph. Good luck telling it apart from similar roads in Salta and La Rioja! The best method may be the clouds: This road has no clouds, while the one in La Rioja has some low hazy ones to the South (except when it doesn't) and the one in Salta has higher, better defined clouds. It's tough.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Tucuman mist road
text: On the 65 in Tucuman, leading west to the Catamarca border near Parque Nacional Aconquija, the Google car drove through what appears to be mist thick enough to clog your windpipe.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Salta red mountains
text: On the 68 in Salta, between Alemania and Cafayate, there's a stretch of red mountains. Compared to the red mountains in La Rioja and Catamarca, the surrounding range is more massive and the red not quite as cartoonish. You may also be able to tell the difference by the clouds: The ones here are high above and relatively defined; the ones in La Rioja, when they appear, are low in the southern sky and kind of hazy, and the coverage in Catamarca is cloudless.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Neuqén sunrise
text: In the North of Neuquén, the Google driver started their day early and the camera did not like it. As the day progresses, the car goes further north and the glitchy colors fade, until only a bit of color noise remains, and finally, around the province border, it starts to look like normal footage.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Caranday Wax Palm
text: Coperinicia alba, also known as the Caranday Wax Palm, have **short, fan-like leaves** that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Caranday Palm
text: Trithrinax Campestris, or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de Córdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves with a trunk hidden by a **coat of dead-leaves.**

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Butia Yatay Palm

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Macaw Palm

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Cardón

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Toothpick Cactus

clues.title: Route marker: Kilometre Markers
text: Argentinian kilometre markers are typically white with a black strip displaying the road number at the top.
The markers on national highways are indicated with RN, while RP indicates a provincial highway.
National highways will be labelled white on the map, while provincial highways will be labelled green.

clues.title: Pole: Poles
text: Round concrete poles sustaining three electricity lines in an alternating pattern are very common in Argentina.
Doubled up poles are also a good clue for Argentina.
Similar doubled concrete poles can occasionally be found throughout Bolivia.

clues.title: Plate: License Plates
text: **Argentina uses two types of licence plates:**
A black one, which will be visible on street view with a black dot in the middle.
A white one with a blue bar at the top.
The black dot can only be found on Argentinian licence plates, while the blue bar can be found in Brazil as well.

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Poplar Plantation - Mediterranean
text: Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.

If you see them planted in single rows accompanied by hilly to mountainous, mediterranean landscape, as well as mediterranean agriculture (e.g. vineyards and olives) and vegetation (e.g. palm trees, platanus trees), you are likely in a town or city in the provinces of Mendoza and San Juan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Azorella Prolifera - Light Green
text: Azorella Prolifera is a plant that looks like "cushions". It is found throughout Patagonia. It's appearence depends on season.
You can see this plant in a distinctive light green color in these regions:
Southern Neuquen
Rio Negro on the roads Chasico-Laguna Blanca and Chasico-Ingeniero Jacobacci
Chubut in the area between Paso del Sapo and Gobernador Costa
Also Chubut on the National 40, south of Rio Mayo, as well as the provincial 55 branching east of the 40.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Single Row Poplar - Flat
text: Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.
If you see them planted in a single row and accompanied by a very flat landscape, you are in one of these places:
National 22 between Neuquen and Choele Choel (Rio Negro)
Trelew (Chubut)
Sarmiento (Chubut)

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Red Baron - Dense
text: Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue.
In very dense assemblages, it can appear here:
Max South Santa Cruz, latitudes south of Rio Gallegos
The national 40 north of Las Horquetas (Santa Cruz)
The national 40 between Esquel and Estanzia Nueva Lubecka
